svg.title: Inside Motion Lab vehicles.js
svg.desc: Method-level behaviour of Vehicle: construction and mode installation, force application and integration, Classic ship aim correction, world-space vertices, and boundary-facing contact selection.
svg.text: Inside vehicles.js
What each method does: install a mode, advance its motion, and calculate its world-space geometry.
1 · CONSTRUCTION AND INSTALL(MODE)
Keep the body; replace the mode’s components
constructor(body): save body + baseInertia; install('car')
install(mode) calls configurations[mode]() for fresh objects.
Assign the returned shell and dynamics, and record the mode.
Use mass × shell.inertiaPerMass if the shell supplies it;
otherwise restore baseInertia. Clear accumulated force and torque.
Position, velocity, angle and angular velocity are preserved by install().
The three configuration factories
car → RectangleShell + CarDynamics
ship → BarbellShell + ShipDynamics(shell.craft)
brick → RectangleShell + ManualForceDynamics
The ship’s craft point is its thrust attachment.
Every call constructs a new pair, even when reinstalling the same mode.
2 · UPDATE(CONTROLS, DT) · EXECUTION ORDER
A · Apply the selected behaviour
dynamics.applyForces(body, controls, dt)
Accumulate this step’s forces and torque.
Uses the currently installed dynamics object.
B · Save angle, then integrate
previousAngle = body.angle
body.integrate(dt)
Advance translation and rotation using physics.js.
C · Correct Classic ship aim
headAngle -= body.angle − previousAngle
Wrap modulo 2π. Ship + Classic mode only.
Preserve world aim through actual body rotation,
including angular acceleration from this step.
3 · WORLDPOINTS() · RETURN TRANSFORMED SHELL VERTICES
Car / Brick: transform each local point
return shell.points.map(p → body.toWorld(p))
The body transform rotates, then translates.
Returns new world-space points; the stored shell vertices remain unchanged.
Ship: rotate the head around its craft point first
p = craft + rotate(p − craft, dynamics.headAngle)
Then apply body.toWorld(p) to the adjusted vertex.
These are the triangular head’s vertices, not the counterweight circle.
4 · SUPPORTPOINT(NORMAL) · RETURN THE BOUNDARY-FACING CONTACT LOCATION
Flat face → midpoint contact
normal
Average tied points on the contacting face.
Avoid artificial spin from choosing just one corner.
The normal points inward; choose the minimum projection
1. Start with worldPoints(). For Ship, also add the counterweight’s surface point:
body.toWorld(shell.counterweight) − normal × shell.radius
2. Find the minimum dot(point, normal); collect points within 1e-8 of it.
3. Return their average: sum of contact points divided by the contact count.
This method selects a location; it does not apply a collision impulse.
Additional exports: shell and dynamics classes, plus ORIGINAL_ENGINE_FORCE, remain available through this module.
